newsitem.title: POLAND: Shareholders of Polish Srubena approve EBRD issue.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders of Polish Srubena approve EBRD issue.

text.p: Shareholders of the Polish screw-maker Srubena SA approved two new issues worth $4 million each, one of which would be taken by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Srubena's president said.

Bogumil Banas told Reuters on Thursday the B and C series would have 1,724,289 shares each. Srubena, located in the southern town of Zywiec now has a capital of 16.96 million zlotys ($5.95 million) divided into 1,580,000 shares.

The C series rights issue would be offered to Srubena's current stockholders -- 15 National Investment Funds, employees and the state treasury, while the B series would be offered entirely to the EBRD.
"After the EBRD takes up its issue somewhere in mid-1997, it will have a stake of about 32 percent in Srubena," Banas said.
The firm, which employs 1,200, made a six-million-zloty net loss in the first nine months of this year on sales of 58 million zlotys.
Srubena's main shareholder is the National Investment Fund (NFI) No.8, which currently holds 33 percent of the firm and which will stay the biggest stockowner after the rights issue.
